**Finding submitted: compliant (at fallback).**

Section 6.1 is the only covenant restricting our business, and it lands squarely on the playbook fallback rather than failing it:

- **Named product scope** — tied to the defined "Deerskin Products" and specifically named competitors, not an undefined "any competing business."
- **Term only** — no post-term tail on the Company.
- **Effectively capped under 12 months** — § 4.1 gives a one-year term renewing in one-year increments, terminable on 90 days' notice, so we can exit the restriction at will.
- **Carve-outs present** — § 6.2 preserves our own closeout website, and the defined term excludes closeout merchandise and Joan Cook Catalog products; § 8(b) grandfathers Globix.

The field of use is also genuinely narrow — it bars only participation in "any project similar to the Site on the Internet," leaving our catalog, retail and sourcing operations untouched. That is the key point: this rule protects our freedom to operate and buy/build, and that freedom survives intact offline.

Two shortfalls versus the *preferred* position were recorded in the rationale rather than redlined, consistent with the classification semantics: the elastic phrase "companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled," and the absence of an express internal-development/acquisitions carve-out. Worth picking up if the agreement is reopened for other reasons.

One direction check worth surfacing: § 6.3 imposes a **two-year post-term** restriction on HDI. Read in isolation that looks like a walk-away trigger, but it binds the counterparty and favors us, so per the rule's detection guidance it was deliberately not flagged. The asymmetry is in our favor and strengthens the case for leaving § 6.1 alone.
